instructions: Negative Marking: 1/3 mark deducted for wrong 1-mark MCQ, 2/3 mark for wrong 2-mark MCQ.
NO negative marking for MSQ or NAT questions.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the most grammatically appropriate word:
'Had the appellant ______ the statutory deadline, the appeal would not have been dismissed in limine.'
questions.solution: Third conditional structure: 'Had + subject + past participle (met)... would have + past participle'.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the most grammatically appropriate word:
'The judge commended the advocate for his ______ argument, which systematically dismantled the prosecution's case.'
questions.solution: 'Cogent' means clear, logical, and convincing, which fits an argument that successfully dismantled opposing claims.

questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'meticulous'.
questions.solution: 'Meticulous' means showing great attention to detail; 'painstaking' carries the same sense of careful, detailed effort. (A) Careless and (D) Indifferent are near-opposites in meaning. (C) Hasty (done quickly, without care) is also broadly opposite in spirit to meticulous.

questions.question: s: (1) All combine harvesters are machines. (2) Some machines are tractors. Conclusions: I. Some combine harvesters are tractors. II. Some tractors are machines. Which conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statements?
questions.solution: Statement (2), 'Some machines are tractors', can always be logically converted to 'Some tractors are machines' — so conclusion II follows directly. Conclusion I does not necessarily follow: 'combine harvesters' is only one subset of 'machines', and nothing guarantees this particular subset overlaps with the subset that are tractors. (A) wrongly accepts I. (C) wrongly accepts both. (D) wrongly rejects the valid conversion in II.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the most grammatically appropriate word:
'Seldom ______ such unanimity among constitutional bench jurists on a contentious matter of public interest.'
questions.solution: Negative inversion: sentences beginning with restrictive adverbs like 'Seldom' require inverted auxiliary-subject word order ('has there been').

questions.question: Two investment funds, Alpha and Beta, yield annual compound returns of 12% and 17% respectively. If an institutional endowment invests ₹10,00,000 divided between the two funds such that both investments yield identical total interest after 2 years (with annual compounding), what is the ratio of capital invested in Fund Alpha to Fund Beta?
questions.solution: Let capital be C1 and C2. Total interest after 2 years is C1 × [(1 + r1)² - 1] = C2 × [(1 + r2)² - 1]. Therefore C1/C2 = [(1 + r2)² - 1] / [(1 + r1)² - 1] = 0.3689 : 0.2544.

questions.question: The ratio of the present ages of a father and his son is 7:2. After 10 years, the ratio of their ages will be 9:4. What is the son's present age, in years?
questions.solution: Let father's age = 7x and son's age = 2x. After 10 years: (7x+10)/(2x+10) = 9/4. Cross-multiplying: 4(7x+10) = 9(2x+10) → 28x + 40 = 18x + 90 → 10x = 50 → x = 5. Son's present age = 2x = 10 years. (A), (C) and (D) arise from sign or cross-multiplication errors while solving the linear equation.

questions.question: Two investment funds, Alpha and Beta, yield annual compound returns of 13% and 18% respectively. If an institutional endowment invests ₹10,00,000 divided between the two funds such that both investments yield identical total interest after 2 years (with annual compounding), what is the ratio of capital invested in Fund Alpha to Fund Beta?
questions.solution: Let capital be C1 and C2. Total interest after 2 years is C1 × [(1 + r1)² - 1] = C2 × [(1 + r2)² - 1]. Therefore C1/C2 = [(1 + r2)² - 1] / [(1 + r1)² - 1] = 0.3924 : 0.2769.

questions.question: In a certain code, FARM is written as HCTO. Following the same coding pattern, how is SEED written?
questions.solution: Each letter of FARM is shifted forward by 2 positions in the alphabet: F→H, A→C, R→T, M→O, giving HCTO. Applying the same +2 shift to SEED: S→U, E→G, E→G, D→F, giving UGGF. (B), (C) and (D) apply an inconsistent or wrong shift to one or more letters.

questions.question: A square sheet of paper is folded in half twice — first vertically, then horizontally — to form a smaller square of one-quarter the original area. A single small triangular notch is then cut from one corner of the folded square. [Figure description: after the two folds, the folded square's four corners correspond, on the original unfolded sheet, to: (i) the centre of the original sheet, (ii) the midpoint of one edge, (iii) the midpoint of the adjacent edge, and (iv) one outer corner of the original sheet. The notch is cut only at the corner in position (i), i.e., the corner that all four folded layers share at the centre.] When the paper is unfolded, how many triangular holes appear, and where are they located?

options.A: One hole, at the centre of the original sheet
options.B: Two holes, symmetric about the centre
options.C: Four holes, one in each quadrant, symmetric about the centre
options.D: Four holes, all at the outer corners

questions.solution: The corner cut corresponds to the point where all four folded layers coincide at the sheet's centre. Cutting through all four layers there produces one small triangular hole in each of the four quadrants of the unfolded sheet, arranged symmetrically about the centre. (A) and (B) underestimate the number of layers cut through. (D) misidentifies which corner of the fold the notch was cut from.

questions.question: Evaluate: lim(x→0) [ (sin 3x) / (tan 5x) ]
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): As x→0, sin 3x ≈ 3x and tan 5x ≈ 5x, so the limit = 3x/5x = 3/5 = 0.6. (A), (C) and (D) result from using the wrong coefficients (e.g., 5/3 inverted, or treating sin and tan as equal to x with the same coefficient).

questions.question: What is the integrating factor for the linear first-order differential equation dy/dx + (2/x)y = x³, for x > 0?
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Integrating factor = exp(∫(2/x)dx) = exp(2 ln x) = x². (A) uses only one power of the coefficient. (C) confuses the integrating factor with the right-hand side term. (D) inverts the sign of the exponent.

questions.question: What are the order and degree, respectively, of the differential equation d²y/dx² + (dy/dx)³ + y = 0?
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): The order is the highest derivative present, which is d²y/dx² (order 2). The degree is the power of the highest-order derivative term once the equation is a polynomial in derivatives, which here is 1 (d²y/dx² appears to the first power). (B) mistakes the exponent on the lower-order term (dy/dx)³ for the degree. (C) and (D) swap or misidentify order and degree.

questions.question: A bag contains 4 red and 6 green balls. Two balls are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that both balls drawn are red?
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): P(both red) = (4/10) × (3/9) = 12/90 = 2/15. (A) results from an arithmetic slip in the multiplication. (C) and (D) result from using the wrong denominator (e.g., not reducing the pool after the first draw, or drawing with replacement).

questions.question: The mean of a set of 8 observations is 15. If one observation of value 25 is removed from the set, what is the mean of the remaining 7 observations? (Round off to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Sum of the original 8 observations = 8 × 15 = 120. After removing 25, the sum of the remaining 7 observations = 120 − 25 = 95. New mean = 95/7 = 13.57.

questions.question: In a simple gear train used in a seed-cum-fertilizer drill, a driver gear with 20 teeth meshes with a driven gear having 60 teeth. If the driver gear rotates at 300 rpm, what is the speed of the driven gear?
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): For meshing gears, N₂ = N₁ × (T₁/T₂) = 300 × (20/60) = 100 rpm. (A) and (C) invert or misapply the teeth ratio. (D) multiplies instead of dividing by the ratio.

questions.question: In a seed drill, the term 'seed rate' refers to:

options.A: The forward speed of the drill during sowing
options.B: The quantity of seed sown per unit area of land
options.C: The number of seed-drop openings per row
options.D: The depth of seed placement below the soil surface

questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Seed rate is defined as the quantity (mass) of seed sown per unit area of land, usually expressed in kg/ha. (A), (C) and (D) describe other operational or design parameters of a seed drill, not the seed rate itself.

questions.subtopic: Cost Analysis of Implements and Tractors
questions.question: The fixed costs of operating a farm tractor include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Fixed costs are incurred irrespective of the extent of tractor use — depreciation, interest on investment, insurance, and taxes are all fixed costs. Fuel and lubricant cost varies directly with hours of operation and is therefore a variable (operating) cost, not a fixed cost.

questions.question: Which of the following is classified as a non-renewable source of farm power?
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Diesel is derived from petroleum, a fossil fuel that is finite and non-renewable. Biogas, solar, and wind are all renewable energy sources commonly used in agriculture.

questions.subtopic: Tractors & Power Tillers — Traction & Mechanics of Tractor Chassis
questions.question: The ratio of the drawbar pull to the dynamic weight on the driving wheels of a tractor is called:
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): The coefficient of traction is defined as the ratio of the maximum drawbar pull developed to the dynamic (normal) weight on the driving wheels. (A) Slip refers to the relative loss of forward travel due to wheel spin, not a force ratio. (C) and (D) describe different, unrelated performance parameters.

questions.subtopic: Power Transmission (Clutch, Gear Box, Differential, Final Drive, Brakes)
questions.question: In a tractor power transmission system, the component that allows the two rear wheels to rotate at different speeds while turning is the:

(A) The clutch engages/disengages engine power. (C) The final drive provides the last speed reduction and torque increase. (D) The gear box selects the overall speed ratio.

questions.question: The calorific value of diesel is 45,000 kJ/kg and its specific gravity is 0.85. Calculate the calorific value of diesel on a volume basis, in MJ per litre. (Round off to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Mass of 1 litre of diesel = specific gravity × density of water = 0.85 × 1 kg/L = 0.85 kg. Calorific value per litre = 45,000 kJ/kg × 0.85 kg = 38,250 kJ/L = 38.25 MJ/L.

questions.section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
questions.question: In the Universal Soil Loss Equation (USLE), the factor that accounts for the combined effect of ground slope steepness and slope length on soil erosion is:

(A) K is the soil erodibility factor, (B) C is the cover-management factor, and (D) P is the support-practice factor — none of these represent topography.

questions.section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
questions.question: Which of the following erosion-control structures is primarily used to reduce the velocity of concentrated flow in a gully and trap sediment?
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:

(A) Contour bunding and (C) terracing are used on the general land slope to control sheet/rill erosion, while (D) a grassed waterway safely conveys concentrated flow rather than obstructing it.

questions.section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
questions.question: In levelling operations using a level instrument and a levelling staff, the reading taken on a staff held at a point of known elevation, at the start of a levelling operation, is called the:
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): The back sight is the first staff reading taken on a point of known elevation (e.g., a benchmark) after setting up the instrument, and is added to the elevation to obtain the height of the instrument. (A) Foresight is the last reading taken from a setup, on a point whose elevation is being determined. (B) Intermediate sights are readings taken between the back sight and foresight. (D) A change point is the point where both a foresight and a subsequent back sight are taken.

questions.question: The specific speed of a centrifugal pump is a parameter used primarily to:

options.A: Determine the pump's power rating directly
options.B: Classify pump type (radial, mixed, or axial flow) and select suitable impeller geometry

questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Specific speed is a dimensionless (or dimensional index) parameter derived from discharge, head, and rotational speed at the best efficiency point, and is primarily used to classify the pump type and guide impeller design/selection. (A), (C) and (D) describe quantities calculated separately, not the purpose of specific speed.

questions.question: A tube well discharges 25 litres per second. If it operates continuously for 6 hours, calculate the total volume of water pumped, in cubic metres (m³). (Round off to the nearest whole number.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Volume = discharge × time = 25 L/s × (6 × 3600 s) = 25 × 21,600 = 540,000 L = 540 m³.

questions.question: The falling-rate period of drying of an agricultural product is characterized by:

options.A: Constant surface moisture, with drying rate controlled by external air conditions
options.B: Drying rate controlled by internal moisture diffusion within the product
options.C: A drying rate that increases continuously with time
options.D: No change in moisture content with time

questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): In the falling-rate period, the rate of drying is governed by the rate at which moisture can diffuse from the interior of the product to its surface, and the drying rate decreases as moisture content decreases. (A) describes the constant-rate period instead. (C) and (D) do not describe any real drying period.

questions.question: The angle of repose of a granular agricultural material is defined as the angle:

options.A: Between the direction of applied force and the material surface during shear failure
options.B: Made by the free-flowing surface of a heaped pile of the material with the horizontal
options.C: Between the major and minor axes of an individual grain
options.D: At which the material begins to flow under vibration alone

questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Angle of repose is the angle that the sloping (free) surface of a naturally heaped pile of a granular material makes with the horizontal plane. (A) describes an angle of internal friction/shear concept, (C) describes grain shape, and (D) is not a standard definition.

questions.question: A wheat grain has axial dimensions of length 6.0 mm, width 3.2 mm, and thickness 2.8 mm. Calculate its geometric mean diameter, in mm. (Round off to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Geometric mean diameter (GMD) = (L × W × T)^(1/3) = (6.0 × 3.2 × 2.8)^(1/3) = (53.76)^(1/3) ≈ 3.77 mm.

questions.question: A cylindrical grain storage bin has an internal diameter of 4 m and is filled with wheat to a depth of 6 m. If the bulk density of wheat is 780 kg/m³, calculate the mass of wheat stored, in tonnes. (Round off to one decimal place.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Volume of grain = (π/4) × d² × h = (π/4) × 4² × 6 = (π/4) × 96 = 75.40 m³. Mass = volume × bulk density = 75.40 × 780 = 58,810 kg = 58.8 t.

questions.question: A sample of paddy intended for storage weighs 500 g on a wet basis. After complete drying to remove all moisture, it weighs 430 g. Calculate the initial moisture content on a wet basis, in percent. (Round off to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Moisture content (wet basis) = (initial mass − dry mass)/initial mass × 100 = (500 − 430)/500 × 100 = 70/500 × 100 = 14.00%.

questions.question: Pasteurization of milk is primarily intended to:

options.A: Sterilize the milk completely, destroying all microorganisms including spores
options.B: Destroy pathogenic microorganisms and reduce spoilage organisms while retaining most nutritional and sensory qualities
options.C: Increase the fat content of milk
options.D: Remove all enzymes present in raw milk

questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Pasteurization is a mild heat treatment designed to destroy pathogenic and most spoilage microorganisms while preserving the nutritional value, flavour, and other sensory qualities of milk. (A) describes sterilization, a more severe process. (C) and (D) are not the purpose of pasteurization.

questions.question: Which of the following statement(s) regarding food preservation methods is/are correct?

options.A: Canning relies on hermetic sealing combined with heat treatment to destroy spoilage microorganisms
options.B: Freezing preserves food primarily by increasing the water activity within the product
options.C: Osmotic dehydration reduces water activity by using a concentrated solution (e.g., sugar or salt) to draw water out of the food
options.D: Irradiation preserves food solely by raising its temperature to destroy microorganisms

questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Canning combines hermetic (airtight) sealing with a heat process sufficient to destroy spoilage and pathogenic organisms, confirming (A). Freezing lowers, not increases, the water activity of a product by converting free water into ice, so (B) is incorrect. Osmotic dehydration uses a concentrated solution to draw water out of food by osmosis, lowering water activity, confirming (C). Irradiation is a non-thermal preservation method that inactivates microorganisms through ionizing radiation, not primarily by heating, so (D) is incorrect.

questions.question: The value of the definite integral ∫(0 to π/2) sin²x cos x dx is:
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Let u = sin x, du = cos x dx. The integral becomes ∫(0 to 1) u² du = [u³/3] from 0 to 1 = 1/3. (A), (B) and (D) result from errors in the substitution limits or from mis-integrating u² as u²/2 or u.

questions.question: Using the Taylor series expansion of f(x) = eˣ about x = 0, up to and including the term in x³, estimate the value of e^0.3. (Round off to three decimal places.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): eˣ ≈ 1 + x + x²/2 + x³/6. At x = 0.3: 1 + 0.3 + (0.09/2) + (0.027/6) = 1 + 0.3 + 0.045 + 0.0045 = 1.3495 ≈ 1.350.

questions.question: The eigenvalues of the matrix A = [[4, 1], [2, 3]] are:
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Characteristic equation: (4−λ)(3−λ) − (1)(2) = 0 → λ² − 7λ + 10 = 0 → (λ−5)(λ−2) = 0, so λ = 5, 2. (A) uses the diagonal entries directly without solving the characteristic equation. (C) and (D) result from sign or arithmetic errors in expanding the determinant.

questions.question: Find the value of the determinant of the matrix B = [[2, 0, 1], [1, 3, 0], [0, 1, 4]].
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Expanding along the first row: det(B) = 2×(3×4 − 0×1) − 0×(1×4 − 0×0) + 1×(1×1 − 3×0) = 2×12 − 0 + 1×1 = 24 + 1 = 25.

questions.subtopic: Farm Machinery — Tillage & Forces on a Tillage Tool
questions.question: A single mouldboard plough has a width of cut of 30 cm and operates at a depth of 20 cm in a soil with a specific draft resistance of 55 kN/m². Calculate the draft required by the plough, in kN. (Round off to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Draft = specific draft resistance × width of cut × depth of operation = 55 kN/m² × 0.30 m × 0.20 m = 55 × 0.06 = 3.30 kN.

questions.subtopic: Farm Machinery — Tillage & Forces on a Tillage Tool
questions.question: A tractor pulls a disc harrow requiring a draft of 8.5 kN at a forward speed of 6 km/h. Calculate the drawbar power required, in kW. (Round off to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Convert speed: 6 km/h = 6000/3600 = 1.667 m/s. Drawbar power = Draft × speed = 8.5 kN × 1.667 m/s = 14.17 kW.

questions.question: A V-belt drive connects a 15 kW electric motor pulley (300 mm diameter, running at 1440 rpm) to a driven pulley of 450 mm diameter used to run a chaff cutter. Assuming no slip, calculate the speed of the driven pulley, in rpm. (Round off to the nearest whole number.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): For a belt drive with no slip: N₂ = N₁ × (D₁/D₂) = 1440 × (300/450) = 960 rpm.

questions.question: A boom sprayer with 12 nozzles spaced 0.5 m apart is operated at a forward speed of 4 km/h. Each nozzle discharges 0.8 L/min. Calculate the spray application rate, in litres per hectare. (Round off to the nearest whole number.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Effective spray swath width = 12 × 0.5 = 6 m. Total nozzle discharge = 12 × 0.8 = 9.6 L/min. Forward speed = 4 km/h = 4000/60 = 66.67 m/min. Area covered per minute = swath × speed = 6 × 66.67 = 400 m²/min. Application rate = (discharge/area) × 10,000 m²/ha = (9.6/400) × 10,000 = 240 L/ha.

questions.question: A biogas plant produces 15 m³ of biogas per day, having a calorific value of 22 MJ/m³. If this biogas is used in a dual-fuel engine with an overall thermal efficiency of 25%, calculate the useful energy output per day, in MJ. (Round off to the nearest whole number.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Energy content of biogas produced = 15 m³ × 22 MJ/m³ = 330 MJ. Useful energy output = 330 × 0.25 = 82.5 MJ.

questions.subtopic: Tractors & Power Tillers — Traction & Mechanics of Tractor Chassis
questions.question: A tractor weighing 18 kN has 70% of its weight on the rear (driving) wheels. If the coefficient of traction between the tyres and the soil is 0.55, calculate the maximum drawbar pull, in kN. (Round off to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Dynamic weight on driving wheels = 18 × 0.70 = 12.6 kN. Maximum drawbar pull = dynamic weight × coefficient of traction = 12.6 × 0.55 = 6.93 kN.

questions.subtopic: Farm Power — Engine Components & I.C. Engine Systems
questions.question: A four-stroke, single-cylinder diesel engine has a bore of 100 mm and a stroke of 120 mm. Calculate the swept volume of the cylinder, in cm³. (Round off to one decimal place.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Swept volume V = (π/4) × d² × L, with d = 10 cm and L = 12 cm. V = (π/4) × 10² × 12 = (π/4) × 1200 = 942.5 cm³.

questions.question: An engine operates on the ideal Otto cycle with a compression ratio of 8. Taking the ratio of specific heats γ = 1.4, calculate the theoretical thermal efficiency of the cycle, in percent. (Round off to one decimal place.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): For the Otto cycle: η = 1 − 1/r^(γ−1), with r = 8 and γ−1 = 0.4. 8^0.4 = 2.297. η = 1 − 1/2.297 = 1 − 0.4353 = 0.5647, i.e., 56.5%.

questions.question: A tractor operator is exposed to a whole-body vibration with an acceleration of 0.8 m/s² for a continuous duration of 4 hours in a working day. The permissible vibration dose is taken as proportional to (acceleration)² × time. If the acceleration increases to 1.2 m/s², calculate the exposure duration, in hours, that would give the same permissible dose. (Round off to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): For equal dose: a₁²t₁ = a₂²t₂ → 0.8² × 4 = 1.2² × t₂ → 2.56 = 1.44 × t₂ → t₂ = 1.78 h.

questions.section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
questions.question: A small agricultural watershed has an area of 25 hectares and a runoff coefficient of 0.35, and it receives a design rainfall intensity of 60 mm/h. Using the Rational Method, Q = CIA/360 (Q in m³/s, I in mm/h, A in hectares), calculate the peak runoff rate, in m³/s. (Round off to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Q = CIA/360 = (0.35 × 60 × 25)/360 = 525/360 = 1.46 m³/s.

questions.section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
questions.question: In a watershed, the total rainfall in a storm was 80 mm, and the resulting direct runoff depth was 32 mm. If the effective duration of the rainfall producing runoff was 4 hours, calculate the φ-index (phi-index), in mm/h, using the relation: infiltration loss = total rainfall − direct runoff. (Round off to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Infiltration (and other) losses = total rainfall − direct runoff = 80 − 32 = 48 mm. φ-index = total loss / effective duration = 48/4 = 12.00 mm/h.

questions.section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
questions.question: Water flows over a rectangular sharp-crested weir of length 1.5 m under a head of 0.25 m. Using the discharge formula Q = 1.84 L H^1.5 (Q in m³/s, L and H in m), calculate the discharge over the weir, in m³/s. (Round off to three decimal places.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Q = 1.84 × 1.5 × (0.25)^1.5. (0.25)^1.5 = 0.25 × √0.25 = 0.25 × 0.5 = 0.125. Q = 1.84 × 1.5 × 0.125 = 0.345 m³/s.

questions.section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
questions.question: Water flows through a horizontal pipe that gradually contracts from a diameter of 300 mm to 150 mm. The velocity of flow in the 300 mm section is 1.2 m/s. Using the continuity equation, calculate the velocity of flow in the 150 mm section, in m/s. (Round off to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): By continuity, A₁V₁ = A₂V₂, so V₂ = V₁ × (D₁/D₂)² = 1.2 × (300/150)² = 1.2 × 4 = 4.80 m/s.

questions.section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
questions.question: A field plot of area 400 m² recorded a soil loss of 18 kg during a rainstorm. Express this soil loss rate in tonnes per hectare. (Round off to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Soil loss per m² = 18/400 = 0.045 kg/m². Soil loss per hectare (10,000 m²) = 0.045 × 10,000 = 450 kg/ha = 0.45 t/ha.

questions.section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
questions.question: A saturated soil sample has a bulk unit weight of 19.5 kN/m³ and a water content of 25% (dry-weight basis). Given the unit weight of water as 9.81 kN/m³, calculate the dry unit weight of the soil, in kN/m³. (Round off to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Dry unit weight γ_d = γ_bulk / (1 + w) = 19.5 / (1 + 0.25) = 19.5/1.25 = 15.60 kN/m³.

questions.question: A confined aquifer of 12 m thickness has a coefficient of permeability of 30 m/day. A fully penetrating well is pumped at a steady rate of 1500 m³/day. The drawdowns observed in two observation wells at radial distances of 15 m and 60 m from the pumped well are s₁ and s₂ respectively. Using the Thiem equation, Q = 2πKb(s₁ − s₂)/ln(r₂/r₁), calculate (s₁ − s₂), in metres. (Round off to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Rearranging the Thiem equation: (s₁ − s₂) = Q × ln(r₂/r₁) / (2πKb). ln(60/15) = ln 4 = 1.386. Denominator = 2π × 30 × 12 = 2261.9. (s₁ − s₂) = 1500 × 1.386 / 2261.9 = 2079.4 / 2261.9 = 0.92 m.

questions.question: For a loam soil with a field capacity of 28% and a permanent wilting point of 12% (both on a dry-weight basis), and a bulk density of 1.4 g/cm³, which of the following statement(s) is/are correct regarding the available water?

options.A: The available water content on a mass basis is 16%
options.B: The available water content on a mass basis is 40%
options.C: The available water depth for a 1 m root zone is approximately 224 mm
options.D: The available water depth for a 1 m root zone is approximately 160 mm

questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Available water content (mass basis) = FC − PWP = 28% − 12% = 16%, confirming (A) and ruling out (B). Available water depth = (FC − PWP)/100 × bulk density × root-zone depth = 0.16 × 1.4 × 1000 mm = 224 mm, confirming (C) and ruling out (D).

questions.topic: Irrigation Water Conveyance and Application Methods
questions.subtopic: Irrigation Water Conveyance and Application Methods
questions.question: An irrigation stream of 40 litres per second is applied to a border strip and is cut off after 90 minutes. If the water infiltrated into the root zone within the field is 150 m³, calculate the application efficiency, in percent. (Round off to one decimal place.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Water applied = 40 L/s × (90 × 60 s) = 40 × 5400 = 216,000 L = 216 m³. Application efficiency = (water stored in root zone / water applied) × 100 = (150/216) × 100 = 69.4%.

questions.question: A subsurface drainage system is to be designed using the steady-state equation S² = 4Kh(2D + h)/q, where S is the drain spacing (m), K is the hydraulic conductivity = 0.5 m/day, h is the height of the water table above the drains at the midpoint = 0.6 m, D is the depth of the equivalent impermeable layer below the drains = 2 m, and q is the drainage coefficient = 0.01 m/day. Calculate the drain spacing S, in metres. (Round off to one decimal place.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): S² = 4 × 0.5 × 0.6 × (2×2 + 0.6) / 0.01 = 4 × 0.5 × 0.6 × 4.6 / 0.01 = 5.52/0.01 = 552. S = √552 = 23.5 m.

questions.question: A batch of paddy weighing 1000 kg (wet basis) with an initial moisture content of 22% (wet basis) is to be dried to a final moisture content of 13% (wet basis). Calculate the mass of water to be removed, in kg. (Round off to one decimal place.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Mass of dry matter (constant during drying) = 1000 × (1 − 0.22) = 780 kg. Final total mass at 13% moisture = 780/(1 − 0.13) = 780/0.87 = 896.6 kg. Water removed = 1000 − 896.6 = 103.4 kg.

questions.question: During the constant-rate period of drying of a food product, the drying rate is 0.15 kg water/(kg dry solid·h). A sample containing 4 kg of dry solid is dried, entirely within the constant-rate period, from a moisture content of 0.80 kg water/kg dry solid to 0.50 kg water/kg dry solid. Calculate the time required, in hours. (Round off to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Water removed per kg dry solid = 0.80 − 0.50 = 0.30 kg/kg. Total water removed = 0.30 × 4 = 1.2 kg. Time = total water removed / (drying rate × dry solid mass) = 1.2/(0.15 × 4) = 1.2/0.6 = 2.00 h.

questions.question: In the size reduction of agricultural materials, which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?

options.A: Rittinger's law assumes the energy required for size reduction is proportional to the new surface area created
options.B: Kick's law assumes the energy required is proportional to the square of the reduction ratio
options.C: Bond's law states that the energy required is inversely proportional to the square root of the product particle size, minus that of the feed particle size
options.D: Hammer mills reduce material size primarily through shearing action between two smooth rollers

questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Rittinger's law states that the energy required for size reduction is directly proportional to the new surface area created, confirming (A). Kick's law actually relates energy to the logarithm of the size-reduction ratio, not its square, so (B) is incorrect. Bond's law expresses energy input as proportional to 1/√(product size) − 1/√(feed size), confirming (C). Hammer mills reduce size primarily by impact (repeated blows from rotating hammers), not by shearing between smooth rollers (which describes roller mills), so (D) is incorrect.

questions.question: A belt conveyor, 500 mm wide, moving at 1.2 m/s, carries grain forming a uniform cross-sectional area of 0.025 m² on the belt. Given the bulk density of the grain as 750 kg/m³, calculate the conveying capacity, in tonnes per hour. (Round off to one decimal place.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Volumetric flow rate = cross-sectional area × belt speed = 0.025 × 1.2 = 0.03 m³/s. Mass flow rate = 0.03 × 750 = 22.5 kg/s = 22.5 × 3600 = 81,000 kg/h = 81.0 t/h.

questions.question: A flat slab of a food product, 4 cm thick, has a thermal conductivity of 0.5 W/(m·K). Under steady-state conditions, the temperature on one face is 60°C and on the other face is 20°C. Calculate the heat flux through the slab, in W/m². (Round off to the nearest whole number.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): By Fourier's law of conduction: q = k × ΔT / L = 0.5 × (60−20) / 0.04 = 0.5 × 40/0.04 = 500 W/m².

questions.question: 1000 kg of milk is to be cooled from 35°C to 5°C in a plate heat exchanger. Taking the specific heat of milk as 3.9 kJ/(kg·K), calculate the total heat to be removed, in MJ. (Round off to the nearest whole number.)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Heat to be removed Q = m × c × ΔT = 1000 × 3.9 × (35−5) = 1000 × 3.9 × 30 = 117,000 kJ = 117 MJ.

questions.question: Which of the following statement(s) about the thermal processing of food is/are correct?

options.A: The D-value (decimal reduction time) represents the time required at a given temperature to reduce the microbial population by 90% (one log cycle)
options.B: The z-value represents the temperature change required to change the D-value by one log cycle (i.e., by a factor of 10)
options.C: A higher D-value indicates that the microorganism is less heat-resistant
options.D: The 12D concept, commonly applied to Clostridium botulinum in low-acid canned foods, refers to a process that reduces the spore population by 12 orders of magnitude (log cycles)

questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): The D-value is, by definition, the time at a fixed temperature needed to achieve a 90% (one log cycle) reduction in microbial population, confirming (A). The z-value is the temperature increase required to reduce the D-value by a factor of 10 (one log cycle), confirming (B). A higher D-value means a longer time is needed for a 90% reduction, indicating the organism is MORE heat-resistant, not less — so (C) is incorrect. The 12D concept for Clostridium botulinum specifies a thermal process that reduces the spore population by 12 orders of magnitude (log cycles), confirming (D).
